title: Catholic Bishops Say Oval Office Prayer Video Was 'Exploited' as Political Photo Op
snippet: Catholic bishops expressed regret after footage of a White House prayer meeting with President Donald Trump was released online, claiming the private gathering was weaponized as a campaign photo op ahead of the midterms.
content:
A high-profile Oval Office gathering between President Donald Trump and a group of Catholic bishops has ignited controversy after Church leaders accused the White House of weaponizing a private prayer moment into a partisan campaign video just weeks before the midterm elections.

The meeting, organized through the conservative think tank Heritage Foundation, was intended as a private discussion on immigration enforcement, religious worker visas, and human dignity. However, after White House officials published footage on social media showing 12 clergymen praying over Trump—garnering millions of views—several bishops issued public statements declaring their participation had been exploited.

Bishops Express Deep Regret

Archbishop Jeffrey Grob of Milwaukee issued a public apology on Sunday, expressing deep regret over what he termed a political photo opportunity. Grob clarified that the gathering was in no way an endorsement of Trump or his administration, asserting that the bishops never granted permission for videos or photos to be publicly distributed.

Bishop William Joensen of Des Moines similarly criticized the release, lamenting that the encounter had been used for partisan gain. Denver Archbishop James Golka, who led the prayer, acknowledged the public backlash and reaffirmed that Church doctrine forbids endorsing political candidates or parties, noting he attended simply to offer prayer as a priest.

Fraying Alliances Ahead of the Midterms

The U.S. Conference of Catholic Bishops (USCCB) swiftly distanced itself from the event, clarifying that it had no involvement in organizing the meeting. The friction highlights growing tensions between Catholic leadership and the White House over aggressive immigration enforcement, international military actions, and public clashes with Pope Leo XIV.

Catholic voters remain a pivotal swing demographic in American politics. While Trump won a majority of the Catholic vote in 2024, recent polling indicates a noticeable drop in approval. As both parties battle for control of Congress in the upcoming midterms, the fallout from the Oval Office footage underscores the delicate line religious leaders must tread in Washington.
